key_insight: System 1 models made fast, probability-based decisions, with stronger performance on medical knowledge and text understanding than on clinical judgment or imaging.
clinical_relevance: These models may support narrowly defined clinical tasks, but speed and confidence estimates do not establish safety for autonomous care.
method: Evaluated four models zero-shot on 86 public tasks across 14 clinical domains and 20 languages.
Grouped tasks into six capability tiers and measured AUROC, calibration and language effects.
Compared results with published benchmarks and generative models.
evidence_signal: Across 179,111 cases, mean best-model-per-task AUROC ranged from 0.94 for medical knowledge to 0.69 for volumetric findings; imaging scored 0.09 below text tasks.
watch_item: Language robustness is a concern: accuracy on identical questions fell by up to 39 percentage points from English to Yoruba.
paper_title: The Value of System 1 Models in Medicine
